# secret/env-file-committed

.env file with secrets that git can commit.

A `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.production` (or similar) file that is tracked by git, or not ignored by it, and holds real secret values.

- Default level: `block`.
- Looks at: the project as a whole, across files.
- References: [CWE-798](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html), [CWE-538](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/538.html), OWASP A07:2025.

## Why it matters

An env file in the repository shares every secret in it with everyone who can read the code, and git keeps it in history. Agents often create `.env` files and commit everything with `git add -A`.

## Flagged

`.env`:

```sh
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-...MsGg
```

`.env.local`:

```sh
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_...DIMR
```

`apps/web/.env`:

```sh
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=eyJ...8PcX
```

`config/.env.production`:

```sh
JWT_SECRET=<high-entropy>
```

## Not flagged

- `OPENAI_API_KEY=your-openai-key-here` in `.env.development`: placeholders only
- `OPENAI_API_KEY=` in `.env.example`: example files are meant to be committed
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=https://acme.dev` in `.env.production`: only public values
- `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-...Cvdv` in `.env.staging`: ignored by .gitignore, so git will not commit it
- `DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/test` in `.env.test`: test env files hold test values and are meant to be committed

## How to fix

Add the file to .gitignore, remove it from git with `git rm --cached <file>`, commit a `.env.example` with empty values instead, and rotate the secrets it held.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore secret/env-file-committed: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "secret/env-file-committed": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).
